Notes

恨意油然而生

油然而生 describes a feeling arising spontaneously. In his April 2025 Dazed interview, Jackzebra said the hostility toward him had increased alongside his audience. That is useful context for this verse’s move from coming first to attracting hate, without identifying any one person as its target.

  • Jackzebra interviewed by Dazed, April 2025
  • Lyric text
酸掉牙

酸 means sour, but it also describes envy in Chinese internet speech: someone else's success can leave a sour taste. The lyric pushes that taste into an exaggerated bodily image—sour enough to make your teeth fall out—immediately after boasting about coming first and attracting hate.

  • People's Daily Overseas Edition: internet slang, 2019
  • Chinese lyric transcript
油炸过的一本书

The next three images all belong to writing: a book, its title and its words. They become deep-fried, withered and insecure. Read as a sequence, they turn contempt into a grotesque little portrait of a text. The book itself is unnamed.

  • Chinese lyric transcript
嘻嘻不嘻嘻

嘻嘻 / 不嘻嘻 is a Chinese internet meme built around a sudden reversal: laughing a moment ago, then no longer laughing. Southern Weekly explained the paired expression in July 2024. Here it follows graphic threats, turning a familiar comic mood-switch into a taunt.

  • Southern Weekly / Nanfang Plus: the 嘻嘻不嘻嘻 meme, July 2024
  • Chinese lyric transcript
瞧不起

The song begins above the earth, looking down on everything; 瞧不起 then means regarding somebody as beneath you. English “look down on” preserves this movement from physical elevation to social contempt. The broad aerial view narrows into a refusal to recognize one particular “you.”

  • Lyric text
心会动不动

心动 commonly means being emotionally stirred or attracted. This line spreads those words around a verb for possibility: a heart that may or may not move. After the dismissal of another person's pain, 'still beats' emphasizes bodily menace, while an emotional echo remains available in Chinese.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 心動
  • Chinese lyric transcript
不服不行

服 here means accepting someone’s ability or superiority, not merely obeying. 不服不行 literally says that refusing to acknowledge it will not do: the listener is denied even the option of withholding respect. It is a sharper boast than simply saying “I am good.”

  • Lyric text
抱团取暖

The literal image is bodies grouping together against the cold. Here it sits beside “losers” and the next line’s resource-swapping, making mutual support sound like a closed circle protecting itself. The same phrase returns beside “little cliques” in “Monoplay.”

  • Monoplay lyric text
  • Lyric text
牛逼

牛逼 is vulgar praise for being impressive, formidable, or exceptionally good. Translating its component characters literally would lose the meaning. Its approving force also contrasts with the abusive 狗逼 earlier in the song: compounds containing 逼 do not all carry the same judgment.

  • Lyric text
摊牌了我不装了

摊牌 means laying your cards face up, and by extension revealing your position or what you have been keeping back. 我不装了 adds 'I'm done pretending.' Together they make a theatrical reveal: the repeated boasts are now out in the open.

  • Ministry of Education dictionary: 攤牌
  • Chinese lyric transcript
